---
id: SA-0317
title: "A PACKAGE raise's mark still counts toward the breaker; its own comment implied otherwise"
type: bug
priority: 3
estimated_lines: 48
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - saffron/task.py
  - tests/test_batch.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - images/**
  - harness/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/cli.py
  - saffron/ledger.py
  - saffron/scheduler.py
  - saffron/reconcile.py
  - saffron/preflight.py
  - saffron/batch.py
  - saffron/phases/**
  - saffron/record/**
  - saffron/gates/**
  - saffron/cell/**
  - saffron/repos/**

  - tests/test_cli.py
  - tests/test_scheduler.py
  - tests/test_queued_specs.py
budget_usd: 6
max_attempts: 2
max_turns: 30
risk: standard
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      The comment `run_task` carries beside its
      `mark_raised_in_package(exc)` call for a `READY_FOR_REVIEW` cell's
      `PackageError` (`saffron/task.py:900-901`) says the mark lets a
      batch "not count this as an ordinary abort." That is false:
      `saffron/batch.py`'s `_drive` runs `consecutive_aborts += 1`
      (`saffron/batch.py:312`) unconditionally, before it ever reads
      `marked = raised_in_package(exc)` (`saffron/batch.py:317`). The mark
      changes only which stop reason a batch closes on, forcing
      `INFRASTRUCTURE` (`saffron/batch.py:1024-1025`) — it does not exempt
      the raise from the breaker. An unmarked raise followed by a marked
      one still trips the breaker at two, the same as two raises of
      either kind alone, and a third candidate queued behind them never
      runs.
    witness: tests/test_batch.py::test_a_marked_raise_shares_the_breakers_tally_with_an_ordinary_one
    wrong_versions:
      - "`_drive` reads `raised_in_package(exc)` before `consecutive_aborts += 1` and skips the increment when the raise is marked, so the marked raise leaves the tally at one and the third candidate runs."
      - "`_drive` increments `consecutive_aborts` at line 312 as usual, but then nets the increment back out to zero when `marked` is `True` by setting `consecutive_aborts -= 1` right after the `if marked:` block, so a marked raise never advances the tally for good and the second candidate's marked raise leaves it at one instead of two, letting the third candidate run."
      - "`_drive` increments `consecutive_aborts` only inside the `if marked:` branch, so an unmarked raise never advances the tally and the marked raise that follows it never reaches two on its own."
      - "`_drive` increments `consecutive_aborts` by `2` for an unmarked raise and leaves it unchanged for a marked one, so the first candidate's unmarked raise alone already reaches the breaker's threshold, and the breaker trips before the second candidate's marked raise is ever attempted."
---

## Context

Finding against `SA-0316` (origin head `872215b4`): the comment
`run_task` writes just before `mark_raised_in_package(exc)`, for a
`READY_FOR_REVIEW` cell's `PackageError`, reads

> Marked so a batch can name `saffron package` as the fix, not count
> this as an ordinary abort (`b-066901`).

at `saffron/task.py:900-901`. "Not an ordinary stop reason" is true: the
mark forces `_promote_in_flight` to return `INFRASTRUCTURE`
(`saffron/batch.py:1024-1025`) whatever the loop's own reason was.
"Not counted as an abort" is false: `_drive`'s `except Exception` branch
runs `consecutive_aborts += 1` (`saffron/batch.py:312`) first, and only
after that reads `marked = raised_in_package(exc)` (`saffron/batch.py:317`).
The marked raise adds to the same tally an unmarked one would, with no
branch anywhere that skips the increment for it. `SA-0316`'s own spec
file gets this right in its own planning prose, naming criterion 2's
witness: "The marked raise still counts toward the breaker, as every
raise does (`saffron/batch.py:298`). Leave that count alone. Criterion
2 drives it."
(`.saffron/specs/SA-0316-a-batch-whose-package-raised-still-exits-0.md:361-362`
— prose in the spec file itself, not a docstring `_drive` or anything
else in `saffron/batch.py` carries), and
`tests/test_batch.py::test_a_batch_whose_package_raised_closes_infrastructure_whatever_it_stopped_on`'s
last block proves the two-marked-raises case. Neither proves the mixed
case — a marked raise and an unmarked raise together — and only the
comment beside the mark itself states the two halves wrong enough to
read as one wrong claim: it is the comment a later editor of this exact
branch would read first.

`consecutive_aborts` is a plain local variable inside `_drive`
(`saffron/batch.py:205-223`), mutated only at lines 312, 357 and 365,
and returned to its caller as the second element of the tuple `_drive`
hands back (every `return reason, consecutive_aborts` in the function,
including line 977's recursive call for the next stack-batch
generation). `_promote_in_flight` (`saffron/batch.py:1004-1027`) runs
once, afterward, from `_stop` (`saffron/batch.py:1029-1043`) or from the
caller directly at line 996 — strictly after `_drive` has already
returned its final tally — and its own signature takes no
`consecutive_aborts` argument at all: it only ever rewrites the stop
*reason* string, never the count. Any wrong build that only touches
`_promote_in_flight` is indistinguishable from the correct build on
every scenario, this spec's witness included, because nothing downstream
of `_drive`'s return ever feeds back into the loop that produced it.
The miscounts this spec guards against are the ones a later editor would
plant inside `_drive` itself, around its three real mutation sites.

`saffron/batch.py:78` fixes `_BREAKER_THRESHOLD = 2`, and the check at
`saffron/batch.py:279` (and again at `saffron/batch.py:253`, once
`pending` runs out) reads `consecutive_aborts` before the next
candidate's own task starts, never after. An unconditional `+= 1` per
raise means the tally reaches `2` after exactly two raises regardless
of order, and a mixed pair — one marked, one unmarked, in *either*
order — reaches it exactly as fast as two raises of the same kind.
This matters for how the witness below is built: a mutant that counts
a marked raise as `0` and an unmarked one as `2` happens to land on the
same final tally as the correct count whenever the pair is one marked
raise *followed by* one unmarked raise (both reach `2` right after the
second raise, before either implementation would have started a
third candidate), so that ordering cannot tell the correct count from
that particular wrong one apart. Putting the unmarked raise *first*
exposes it instead: the wrong count reaches `2` after the first raise
alone and trips the breaker before the second candidate — the one
that would have raised the marked exception — is ever attempted, while
the correct count reaches `2` only after both raises and still starts
the second candidate first. The witness below orders its two raises
that way for exactly this reason.

## Problem

1. **Reword the comment.** Replace the two lines at
   `saffron/task.py:900-901` with wording that keeps both halves true:
   the mark routes a batch to `saffron package` and forces the row
   closed `INFRASTRUCTURE`, and `_drive`'s breaker still counts the
   raise toward `consecutive_aborts` like any other, because the
   increment at `saffron/batch.py:312` runs before anything there reads
   the mark. Cite `b-066901` as the existing comment does. Change
   nothing else on those lines: `mark_raised_in_package(exc)` and the
   bare `raise` after it keep their place and their behavior.
2. **Add a witness that pins the corrected reading.** In
   `tests/test_batch.py`, add a test that drives `run_batch` over three
   candidates whose first raises a plain, unmarked `CellRuntimeError`
   and whose second raises a marked `CellRuntimeError` (build it with
   the existing `_marked_runtime_error` helper). Assert the returned
   reason is `INFRASTRUCTURE`, that only the first two candidates' ids
   appear in the runner's call order (the third's runner is never
   called), that each of the first two specs gets a `raised` line, that
   only the second spec's id appears beside a `saffron package` command
   line, and that the first spec's id does not. This ordering is what
   lets the witness tell the correct tally apart from the specific wrong
   one described in the fourth `wrong_versions` entry above (see the
   Context section's last paragraph for why the reverse order would not):
   that wrong build already reaches the breaker's threshold off the
   first, unmarked raise alone, so it never even starts the second
   candidate, while the correct build starts both and only then stops
   the third.

## Out of scope

- `saffron/batch.py` itself. Its `_drive`, `_promote_in_flight` and
  `_stop` already increment and promote correctly; this spec is
  forbidden from touching the file and needs no change to it. The
  `wrong_versions` list above names mutations a grader builds against
  `_drive` to check the witness's power to fail them — none of them is
  part of this spec's own diff.
- Every other comment and docstring `SA-0316` wrote. Its module
  docstring, and the docstrings on `_drive`, `wrapped`'s runner handler,
  `_is_layer`, `_promote_in_flight` and `_stop`, already describe a
  marked raise correctly; only the one comment cited above conflates
  the two halves.
- `tests/test_task.py` and `tests/test_cli.py`. Both are reachable
  paths for this follow-up, but the claim here is about `_drive`'s
  tally, not about `run_task`'s own marking (already witnessed by
  `tests/test_task.py::test_a_raise_that_escapes_run_task_from_package_is_marked_and_kept`)
  or about `saffron batch`'s exit code (already witnessed by
  `tests/test_cli.py::test_saffron_batch_exits_2_and_names_the_package_command_when_package_raised`).
  Neither needs a new witness for this finding.
- The exhausted-mode `except BaseException` branch two lines below
  (`saffron/task.py:909-911`). It carries no such comment and is not
  the one the finding names.

## Notes for the agent

The witness is a brand-new test, so it cannot declare `preserves: true`:
`saffron/intake.py`'s own `Criterion.preserves` docstring is explicit
that "a new test can never preserve: it did not pass at base," and
`saffron/gates/core/criteria.py::_judge` enforces exactly that — a
`preserves` criterion whose witness was not already green at `base_sha`
fails every time, and a test absent from `tests/test_batch.py` at base
cannot have been green there. This spec changes no runtime behavior —
only the comment, and `saffron/batch.py` is forbidden — so the claim is
about a tally `_drive` already gets right at base. The criterion is
declared the ordinary way instead: no `preserves`, a witness the suite
never collected at base (so `_judge`'s `witness-green-at-base` branch
cannot fire either, the same as any other brand-new test), and a
`wrong_versions` list naming the specific miscounts a later editor
*would* introduce into `saffron/batch.py`'s `_drive` if they took the
old comment's wrong half at its word — the regression this follow-up's
reworded comment, and this witness, exist to keep out of that forbidden
file, not one this diff itself makes. Each entry mutates one of
`_drive`'s own three mutation sites for `consecutive_aborts` (lines
312, 357, 365); none of them routes through `_promote_in_flight`, which
never sees the counter at all and so cannot be mutated into a build the
witness would distinguish from the correct one. Build the marked
exception with `_marked_runtime_error`, already defined in
`tests/test_batch.py` (it imports `mark_raised_in_package` inside its
own body, so this witness needs no module-scope import of anything
`saffron.task` added). Build the unmarked one as a plain
`CellRuntimeError(...)`, with no mark at all, the same way the existing
`test_a_batch_whose_package_raised_closes_infrastructure_whatever_it_stopped_on`
does at `tests/test_batch.py:895`. Pass no `sleep` argument to
`run_batch`: every call in this file already omits it, and the default
`None` is what keeps an unmarked `CellRuntimeError` from being silently
re-offered instead of counted once and left alone.
